text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
THE STRAITS TIMES:
- ASEAN decides to defer Cambodia's entry into regional grouping "until a later date" because of political crisis in country.

- Cambodian capital tense as foreigners scramble to leave and supporters of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's party either fleeing or falling in line with new regime of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
- Passenger sucked out of Brazilian TAM airplane and fell to his death on Wednesday after an explosion, caused probably by unidentified chemicals, tore hole in fuselage, police said.

- A remisier who had monthly Area Licence Scheme label for his Rolls-Royce car and placed it on his Mercedes-Benz to drive into the restricted zone has been sentenced to two weeks' jail and fined Singapore $800.
- Regional bourses savaged by currency market turmoil caused by recent attacks on Philippine peso and Malaysian ringgit.
- International funds speculating heavily against ringgit lack understanding of region, says Malaysia acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
THE BUSINESS TIMES:
- Bank Negara, Malaysia's central bank, hits ringgit speculators again, pushing interest rates to record highs and sending Kuala Lumpur stock market to 19-month low.
- Malaysia's economic adviser Daim Zainuddin comes out in support of slumping stock market, deflated by flight of funds from region.

- Key challenges that need to be addressed in Friday's budget by Finance Minister Richard Hu are to lower business costs, accelerate economy's transition to high-value activities, and develop high-level skills, Business Times business panel concludes.
- Last-minute spurt of bargain hunting among index-linked counters saves benchmark Singapore stock market index from closing at new 30-month low.

- Singapore may not be able to bring back former Merrill Lynch staffer Kevin Wallace to face trial for crimes he allegedly committed here as its extradition treaty with Hong K Kong lapsed when territory returned to China on July 1, legal sources say.
- Taiwan's Hutong Investment Holdings is set to become second venture capital fund listed on Stock Exchange of Singapore after Transpac Industrial Holdings, listed in 1994.
- NatSteel Electronics, electronics arm of NatSteel, has emerged as buyer of Apple's Singapore printed circuit board assembly assets.

- Block of 14.7 percent of PT Indofood Sukses Makmur shares traded on the Surabaya Stock Exchange on Wednesday, fuelling talk Singapore's QAF may be involved in an impending reshuffle of Salim group assets.
- Sinar Mas group has almost 100 percent of Amcol Holdings under its belt as unconditional offer for company ends.
- Businessman Mirzan Mahathir has received approval to begin talks to buy government's 29.35 percent stake in national shipping firm Malaysia International Shipping Corporation.
-- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
